_comment: C0 body translation · garak (2026-11-06). Key contract per cursor.en.json; sources/related counts must match the source file.

axes.model_access: It ships no model of its own — the thing under test is somebody else's model or application: the repository front page defines generators as "plugins for LLMs to be probed", and names hugging face hub generative models, replicate text models, openai api chat & continuation models, aws bedrock foundation models and litellm, adding "pretty much anything accessible via REST". The documentation's first-scan example is `--model_type huggingface --model_name gpt2`. The full generator list and per-provider parameter differences: not itemised.
axes.runtime: A local Python process with a terminal interface: the README install command is `python -m pip install -U garak`, PyPI records `pip install garak` with requires-python >=3.11, and the "Setting up" doc page likewise describes a command-line tool. Scan requests go to the target endpoint you pick — a cloud API or local inference. Whether a hosted execution surface exists, and the official Docker story: no official text captured in this pass, recorded as unknown.
axes.local_files: It reads the probe datasets installed with the package and your local configuration, and writes local result files: the README records JSONL, garak.log and hit logs; the "Our Features" doc page lists four output kinds — Screen output, Report log, Hit log, Debug log. Default directory names, retention and cleanup rules: not verified word for word in this pass.
axes.background: There is no "keeps running after you shut down" hosted task: one scan is one local process that writes logs when it ends. The docs table of contents lists Setting up, Your first scan and Getting help, with no resume or queue semantics. How batch runs parallelise and throttle: no official text captured in this pass.
axes.tools: Four plugin surfaces (README's own phrasing): probes are "classes for generating interactions with LLMs", detectors are "classes for detecting an LLM is exhibiting a given failure mode", harnesses are "classes for structuring testing", and generators connect to models. Selection syntax appears in the docs example `--probes lmrc.Profanity`, and `--list_probes` enumerates probes. MCP support: not described in the official docs, recorded as unknown.
axes.context: Here "context" means how a harness assembles multiple turns into one probe, not cross-session memory. The README's statement about harnesses stops at "classes for structuring testing"; the concrete conversation-construction and length strategy had no official text captured in this pass, recorded as unknown.
axes.permissions: The licence is unambiguous: Apache-2.0 (LICENSE read directly, see the licence field). There is only one readable official statement about data flow — probe prompts and responses go to the target endpoint you configured, and failing samples are written item by item to local logs (README: "If any of the prompt attempts yielded an undesirable behavior, the response will be marked as FAIL"). Whether telemetry is on by default or results are uploaded: no official statement captured, moved to unknowns. It never blocks live traffic, so there is no "what share it stops" conclusion to write; this site cites no success-rate or miss-rate figures.
axes.fit: Fits: running a probe sweep against an endpoint you control before launch, keeping reviewable prompt/response evidence files rather than a slogan, reusing one probe set across HuggingFace, OpenAI, Bedrock, litellm and other targets. Not a fit: intercepting user requests at runtime (it does not block); reading "all probes PASS" as proof the model is safe (the official framing only records failing samples); teams needing a hosted report platform or compliance certificates.

runs:
**This site has not run it end to end**: no `python -m garak` execution, no JSONL/hit log opened, no scores, success rates or rankings produced, and no probe count tallied. This archive only organises statements on record at the official repository front page, LICENSE, garak.ai, docs.garak.ai and PyPI — item by item in sources with the verification date.

**Suggested measurements** (four, each pointing at something the official readable pages do not give):

- **Comparability across targets**: how the same `--probes` set differs in wall time and failure surface between a local HuggingFace endpoint and a hosted OpenAI-style endpoint
- **Default log directory and retention behaviour** (not spelled out in the official docs; confirm where files land)
- **Whether any telemetry is on by default** (no official statement captured in this pass)
- **Reproducibility under Docker / CI** (no official image statement captured in this pass)
unknowns:
- The complete generator list and per-provider parameter differences (the official pages name only a few)
- Default log directory names, retention and cleanup rules
- Whether telemetry or result upload is on by default (no official statement captured)
- The official Docker image and CI-integration story (no text captured in this pass)
- Harness conversation-construction and length strategy (the README gives one defining sentence only)
- MCP transport support (not described in the official docs)
- Why the releases page date label for v0.17.1 does not fully match PyPI
- Mainland-network direct reachability and filing status (not measured, not searched)
related: Also a red-teaming framework: the PyRIT archive organises orchestration and attack strategies through a Python SDK and a GUI, while this archive's default entry point is a one-shot terminal scan.
Also an evaluation tool that can run in CI: Promptfoo's main axis is prompt/agent assertions and regression, whereas this archive's main axis is attack probes.
A local inference endpoint: Ollama only becomes relevant to garak as one target shape among the generator plugins.
